slides.0.title: Viticulture and climate risk
slides.0.subtitle: Winter freeze, rootstocks, wildfire and disease
slides.1.title: Winter freeze and own-rooted vines
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Eastern Washington
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Continental winter cold snaps have hit vines hard; severe freezes in 1996 and 2003 damaged Merlot and pushed plantings towards Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Own-rooted vines
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Phylloxera risk is low in Washington's sandy soils, so some growers plant ungrafted vines to avoid the frost-vulnerable graft union
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Elsewhere
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The Finger Lakes and Idaho are cold-winter regions; the Finger Lakes rely on the lake effect and snow cover, while Idaho's Snake River Valley gets only 10–12 inches of rain and needs irrigation
slides.1.content: Winter is the core risk inland and in the east; autumn rain is the risk on the maritime west.
slides.2.title: The 2020 wildfires and smoke taint
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The event
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A September 2020 weather event fuelled over 100 major forest fires and burned more than five million acres on the West Coast
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Chemistry
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Volatile phenols in smoke (such as guaiacol and cresols) are absorbed by grapes and can bind to sugars as odourless glycosides that release phenols during fermentation
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Flavour
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Smoky, burnt, ashy or medicinal notes; impact varies by variety and wine style
slides.2.content: Test for volatile phenols and glycosides, then use small-lot ferments and sensory checks to decide on harvest.
slides.3.title: Disease and grape choice
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Southeast Texas
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Pierce's disease has hit vineyards hard; resistant grapes such as Blanc du Bois and Black Spanish are planted more
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Virginia
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Hot, humid summers; Jefferson's vineyards around 1807 failed because of black rot and phylloxera
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Texas High Plains
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Low humidity makes downy mildew, Pierce's disease, phylloxera and black rot uncommon
slides.3.content: Humidity drives disease: the humid East leans on resistant grapes, the dry interior suffers less.
Which variety did the severe freezes of 1996 and 2003 damage most?
Merlot suffered, and plantings shifted to Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc.
Why do some Washington growers plant ungrafted vines?
A. Sandy soils carry little phylloxera risk and it avoids the frost-prone graft union
D. Because rainfall is too high
Sandy soils carry little phylloxera risk.
Which compounds mainly cause smoke taint?
A. Volatile phenols and their glycosides
